Show and manage current AFRd2 status
Fast decision by declared frame rate

Apply the mode immediately from the frame rate declared by the decoder (vdec_status: frame rate) — the way the built-in system AFR does, which is why it switches in 2-4 s. The decision is provisional: our own measurement verifies it, and on mismatch the mode is corrected (see "Frame rate recheck"). 0 — decide by measurement only (slower, but independent of the driver\'s honesty). Off by default on Android 12-14, on by default on Android 10/11.
If the player reports the frame rate itself via the AFRd2 API (frame_rate_hint), prefer it over our own frame counter measurement.

Raising the mode and resetting the player ceiling apply only to the selected applications. Default: the built-in YouTube, the only player where clamping was measured; for some players the ceiling reset restarts the screen and breaks playback. Empty list — nobody.

Raise the display mode to the maximum supported by the TV before the first frame of the player and, if a video still started under a low rate, reset the player\'s rate ceiling by bumping the display density (the player re-reads the mode and delivery recovers without restarting playback). Needed for players that remember the display rate at the start of a video and never raise it (stock YouTube on Android 11+). The cost is one extra mode transition for content that is not at the maximum rate; on Android 10/11 the ceiling reset is not performed (it costs 1.5-2.5 s there). When off, the mode is chosen by measurement only, and a video started under a low rate may stay clamped. Applies only to the players in the list below.

The daemon does not switch the mode until it has collected this many milliseconds of observation. The rate is taken as the minimum over sub-windows (5 s), so short bursts and repeated frames at segment boundaries do not derail the decision. 20000 is the measured optimum: 24 fps YouTube videos are detected correctly in 86 % of cases; 0 — decide from the first sub-window.
How far to extend the observation when the confidence interval does not fit one rate group (larger is more accurate but switches later). Never less than the observation value.

Do not wait for the full observation: if two separated sub-windows yield the same rate class (quorum), the mode is switched already here. Clear content (local files, 50/60 fps) switches earlier, while borderline 24/25 waits for the full observation. 0 — full observation only.
Length of each sub-window the minimum rate is taken over. 5 s is a compromise: over 5 s a ±1 frame counter error is ±0.2 fps at 24 fps.
Sub-windows starting earlier are ignored. Some players under-report the rate while filling the buffer in the first seconds, and the minimum is sensitive to such a dip.
How many times to retry before leaving the mode as is until the end of the video.
If the declared frame duration (frame dur) differs from the measurement by no more than this percent, the decision is taken from it. 0 — disabled.
How many ms after switching to measure again and fix the mode if the class differs (heals a biased first window). 0 — disabled.

How many ms after switching to check the video layer delivery cadence; if frames reach the display twice as rarely (video looks like 13 fps), the mode is switched away and back (a mode change does not re-init the HWC vsync path). 0 — disabled.
How often to check /sys/class/vdec/vdec_status to notice video start and stop.
Delay after video appears, to filter out bounce.

End-of-playback confirmation pause: after the decoder disappears the daemon waits this long and re-checks, so short gaps (seeking, quality switch, splice) are not taken for the end of the file. 0 — confirm immediately (the end is handled sooner, but gaps are taken as the end too). Restoring the mode is controlled by the separate "Restore mode on stop" item.
On — the mode is kept on pause; off — the original mode is restored on pause and set again on resume.
Restore the original HDMI mode when video ends. Disabled — the video mode stays (fewer screen blinks), but apps with their own AFR can change the mode again: the backdoor flag is released anyway.

Some players feed frames to the decoder faster than nominal (e.g. YouTube on a 24 fps video measures ~25.2 fps, so AFR picks 25 Hz). The correction is applied to the measurement before the mode is chosen. On by default: the AV1 correction below is active, the per-player list is empty.

Percent is how much the player over-reports the rate (the same correction the daemon prints as "плеер <пакет>: поправка замера ±P %"). Touch the row and pick the players: the package name is not typed with the remote. Compare with the nominal rate of the video; players the daemon measures correctly need no entry.

Additive correction for the AV1 decoder path over-reporting the frame counter. Measured: AV1 gives +0.5 frames/s versus H.264 on the same file. Default is 0.1 — the largest value at which no tested 25-fps clip slips into 24 Hz (at 0.3 honest 25-fps content already drifts into 24 Hz, at 0.5 even more so). An error of "24 fps detected as 25 Hz" is treated as the lesser evil than the reverse, so the correction is not raised to the measured 0.5; the envelope observation already removes most of the bias. Applied only when player calibration is enabled (see the switch above): with it off the value is neither used nor logged. Android 11-14.
Limit the AV1 correction to one player package (fps.correct.av1.pkg). Empty — any player.
Players that AFR gets in the way of

For the selected applications AFRd2 measures the frame rate and writes everything to the log, but does not switch or hold the display mode. Tap the row and pick applications from the list of installed players. On Android 6-9 the mode is simply not switched for the selected applications — there is no measurement.
No applications found — clear "Video players only" to see all

For the selected applications the daemon avoids display modes below the given rate (Hz): players that clamp their rendering pace when a clip starts in a low mode then behave. Touch the row, tick applications and set the rate right there.
